_read_me_first: Ceilings for test/english-ratchet.test.mjs. A ceiling is the number
of German-flagged lines a tracked text file had when it was last
measured. The test fails if a file's CURRENT count exceeds its
ceiling, or if a file carries German lines with no ceiling entry at
all (a new offender). A count BELOW its ceiling is not a failure —
the test prints a hint to lower that entry, and this file should
then be edited to match, so the ratchet only ever tightens.
'exemptions' are files whose German content is DATA or a
MEASUREMENT RECORD by design, not prose debt, and so are never
ceilinged and never fail — see each entry's own reason.
'filenameAllowlist' is the file-NAME version of the same idea: a
short explicit list of German words (Lucky's decision, 2026-09-26)
must not appear in any tracked path unless it is named here.
metric: German lines per file / total tracked text files, using test/english-dictionary.mjs's two-distinct-word threshold and KNOWN_VERBATIM_QUOTES over EVERY line of EVERY file `git ls-files` tracks (not only comments) — the same rule test/english-only.test.mjs applies to src/bin/test/bench comments, widened to the whole repo per Lucky's 2026-09-26 decision that cheap-mem is throughout-English.

baseline.measured_2026-09-26_by_this_agent: 2348 German lines across 66 of 434 tracked files (52 files/1681 lines ceilinged below, 14 files/667 lines in 'exemptions')
baseline.cited_in_task_2026-09-26_by_lucky: 2406 German lines across 69 files, measured before this branch's dictionary refactor moved test/english-only.test.mjs's inline word list into test/english-dictionary.mjs — that move changed which FILE a few dozen self-referential 'dictionary as data' lines live in and how they wrap, which explains most of the gap; both numbers were produced by the identical dictionary and threshold, re-measuring rather than reusing Lucky's figure is why they differ.

expected: every ceiling in this file only falls or holds — never rises without a matching drop elsewhere; the grand total (ceilings + exemptions) never rises; a file not listed here that gains a German-flagged line becomes a failing new offender, not a silent addition.
abort: the ratchet flags a genuinely English line as German.
